# Workspaces

A workspace is a folder on your computer that you let helpers use. For example, your notes folder.

Helpers can only see the folders you connect. They can read them. They can only change things if you allow it.

Workspaces live in the **Files** view, in a folder called **Workspaces**. It sits next to the Session, Project and Global folders.

## Where a workspace is seen

Inside **Workspaces**, a workspace is under one of these:

- **Session**. Only this chat can use it.
- **Project**. Every chat in this project can use it.
- **Global**. Every chat can use it.

Which of these you see depends on where you opened Files. A chat shows all three (Project only if the chat is in a project). A project shows Project and Global.

## Add a workspace

1. Open **Files**.
2. Right-click **Session**, **Project** or **Global** under **Workspaces**.
3. Choose **New workspace**.
4. Give it a name and choose the folder.

A workspace can be **Writable** or read-only. Read-only means helpers can look but not change.

## Make a temporary workspace

A temporary workspace is an empty folder the app makes for one chat. Helpers can write in it, and each change asks for your OK.

1. Right-click **Session** under **Workspaces**.
2. Choose **New temporary workspace**.
3. Give it a name.

The folder is kept while the chat is in the trash. It is deleted when the chat is deleted for good. To delete it sooner, right-click it and choose **Delete**. If you copy the chat, the copy gets its own copy of the folder.

## Look inside a workspace

Open a workspace in the tree to see its folders and files. Click a file to read it. Text, images and audio can be shown. You cannot change files here. Helpers change them, with your OK, or you change them outside the app.

A very large folder shows only the first 2000 entries, the ones nearest the top first.

## Change a workspace

Right-click the workspace and choose **Settings**. You can change the name, the folder and **Writable**. You can also see:

- **Always allowed**. The tools you chose to always allow in this workspace. Press **Remove** to be asked again.

## Files that .gitignore ignores

If your folder is a git project, helpers do not see the files its `.gitignore` files ignore. Those files are not searched. They do not show up when a helper lists the folder, searches, or reads. If a helper asks for one by name, the answer is that it does not exist. The `.git` folder is never shown.

In **Files**, ignored files are still there. They are dimmed and marked **ignored**, and you can open and read them.

To turn this off for a workspace, open its **Settings** and switch off **Respect .gitignore**.

## Choose what each place can see

Every file and folder of a workspace has a checkbox. It means "visible to" the place you are looking from:

- In a chat's Files: visible to this chat.
- In a project's Files: visible to every chat in the project.
- In Global Files: visible to every chat.

Untick a file to hide it. Helpers in that place do not see it, search it, or read it. A hidden folder hides everything inside it. Everything is visible until you change it, and new files are visible.

A place can hide more than the one above it, but it cannot show what the one above hides. That checkbox is greyed out. For example, a file hidden in Global Files cannot be shown again from a chat.

A hidden file is not searched in that place, even if it is ticked in **Searched parts**. It shows there as unticked and cannot be ticked.

## Choose what helpers can search

In **Settings**, open **Searched parts**. You can tick the whole folder or only some folders and files. Helpers search only what you tick.

Press **Rescan** if you added new files.

## Let a helper run commands

A helper can run shell commands, such as tests or a build, in a **writable** workspace on macOS or Linux. This is for coding work. See [Shell commands](approvals-and-tools.md#shell-commands).

## Use a workspace in a chat

Ask your question. For example, "What do my garden club notes say about seeds?" The helper can use the workspaces of Session, Project and Global.

The helper looks through the folder and answers.

## Changes need your OK

If a helper wants to write a file in your folder, it asks first.

![The helper asks before saving to your folder][approval-workspace]

You can choose:

- **Allow once**
- **Allow for this session**
- **Always allow this tool**
- **Deny**

## Remove a workspace

Right-click it and choose **Move to trash**. Your folder on the computer is not touched. To bring it back, turn on **Show deleted files**, right-click it and choose **Restore**.

A temporary workspace is deleted instead, with its folder.
